newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Britax sees auto component acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Britax sees auto component acquisitions.

text.p: British manufacturer Britax International Plc said on Tuesday its automotive components division expected to make a number of greenfield acquisitions this year as part of its move to double revenue by 2005.
Britax automotive components division manager Mark Selway told reporters the company planned to double annual revenue to around two billion stg largely through acquisitions.
The company this month announced a 72.8 million stg acquisition of German aircraft interior equipment maker Buderus Sell Group from Buderus AG.
Selway said Britax would consider further major acquisitions next year, while his division had four or five smaller acquisitions currently in the pipeline.

"(We have) four to five acquisitions in greenfield sites on the go across the world," he said, adding they would be in new and emerging markets and he expected announcements to be made before the end of the year.
Selway was speaking at the opening here of the division's global research and development centre which will co-ordinate an annual A$20 million production development budget.
With Britax being the world's third biggest supplier of car mirrors, a prime aim of the research centre is to lead world development of products which may one day replace mirrors.
Britax Research director Rob Gilbert said the centre aimed to go well beyond normal product design and manufacture.
"Instead of customer-specific work, Britax Research will undertake advanced research to find completely new ways of doing things and to develop truly revolutionary products," he said.
